clue.text: Fiancee at home looked after

parts.note: someone at home is said to be in
to look after is to tend, so looked after is tended

explanation.surface: A bride-to-be stays in and is cared for.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiancee is the person one plans to marry, called one's intended in old-fashioned usage.

clue.text: Sound reason for noises made by rooks

indicators.note: Sound at the front says the word for reason is to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a reason for something is its cause

explanation.surface: Asking a good explanation for the racket that rooks make.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound reason' reads as 'a valid reason', but 'Sound' signals a homophone of CAUSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Rooks and crows make harsh calls, each written as a caw; several are caws.

clue.text: A revolutionary form of suffering

parts.note: Che Guevara is the crossword's standard revolutionary

explanation.surface: Revolution presented as a kind of torment.
explanation.definitionFit: A dull persistent pain is one kind of physical suffering.

clue.text: In brothers' place it's the main consideration

indicators.note: In tells us the word it goes inside the brothers' house

parts.note: a priory is a house where monks (brothers) live
it gives IT; the 's is just 'is', joining wordplay to definition

explanation.surface: In a monastery, something is the chief concern.
explanation.definitionFit: What gets dealt with first is the matter of greatest importance, the top concern.

clue.text: Craftsman with power, one taking sides

parts.note: P is the standard abbreviation for power in physics
an artisan is a skilled craftsman

explanation.surface: A powerful craftsman who backs one faction.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue lists the craftsman first, but P goes at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A partisan is a committed supporter of one party or cause, so one who takes sides.

clue.text: Greek character in Athens initially digesting sacred books

indicators.note: digesting means the first letters swallow the sacred books
initially takes the opening letter of each of the two words 'in' and 'Athens'

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, a set of sacred books

explanation.surface: A Greek person in Athens is reading scripture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' works on 'in' as well as 'Athens', giving I and A.
explanation.definitionFit: Iota is the ninth letter of the Greek alphabet, a character in the written sense.

clue.text: Be indecisive, though oddly content with his fee

indicators.note: oddly suggests these letters are arranged strangely, a shuffle

explanation.surface: Someone can't decide, even though they're happy with what they're paid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' is the anagram signal working on CONTENT and HISFEE together; 'with' just joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes refusing to choose between two sides, staying undecided.

clue.text: Anger displayed in preliminary round

definitions.meaning: anger is ... in the sense of passion or rage
a qualifying race or round before the final is a ...

explanation.surface: Fury shown during the qualifying stage of a contest.
explanation.definitionFit: Heat means passion or fury, and in athletics it also names an early qualifying race.

clue.text: Horse not out to cross a high peak

indicators.note: to cross means the horse-plus-not-out letters straddle the a

parts.note: a mount is a horse for riding
the opposite of out is in

explanation.surface: A rider on a horse that stays in sets off over a lofty summit.
explanation.definitionFit: A mountain is a very high landform rising to a peak.

clue.text: Unexpected gain is in badges of office

indicators.note: Unexpected means the letters turn up in a surprising order, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A surprise profit lies in the regalia of an official post.
explanation.definitionFit: Insignia are emblems or badges showing someone's rank or position.

clue.text: Partly outgun Italian army division

indicators.note: Partly says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A military formation gets the better of the Italians in part.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit is a body of soldiers forming one subdivision of an army.

clue.text: Make an impression and so on, introducing husband

indicators.note: introducing means the husband is brought in alongside, at the end

parts.note: etc is the abbreviation for et cetera, meaning and so on

explanation.surface: Someone making a mark, then bringing in their spouse.
explanation.definitionFit: To etch is to cut a design into a surface, literally making an impression.

clue.text: Obsession with afternoon meal, say? Babies go through it

indicators.note: say signals the word for the afternoon meal is taken by how it is spoken

parts.note: tea is the British light afternoon meal
to have a thing about something is to be obsessed with it

explanation.surface: Someone obsessed with afternoon tea; infants endure the process.
explanation.walkthrough: The obsession comes first in the clue but last in the answer. Tea is the British afternoon snack of tea and cakes.
explanation.definitionFit: Infants go through the stage of cutting their first teeth, which is called this.

clue.text: Fruit from tree, in can for cooking

indicators.note: cooking means the letters are worked over and mixed up

explanation.surface: Fruit picked from a tree goes into a tin to be cooked.
explanation.definitionFit: The nectarine is a smooth-skinned variety of peach, a stone fruit.

clue.text: Incident involving archdeacon in popular film

indicators.note: involving means the film's letters wrap around the archdeacon

parts.note: ET is Spielberg's hugely popular 1982 film
Ven, short for Venerable, is the title of an archdeacon

explanation.surface: Something happens with a senior cleric in a hit movie.
explanation.definitionFit: An event is something that happens, an occurrence or incident.

clue.text: Place sale items initially in warehouse

indicators.note: in puts those two letters inside the warehouse

parts.note: a depot is a storehouse or warehouse

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letter of both 'sale' and 'items'

explanation.surface: Instructions for stocking up goods for a sale.
explanation.definitionFit: To place something down is to deposit it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Condescend to talk of Hamlet, for one?

indicators.note: to talk of means the word is spoken, so its sound is what counts

parts.note: Hamlet was Prince of Denmark, so an example of a Dane

explanation.surface: Is speaking about Shakespeare's prince beneath one?
explanation.walkthrough: Hamlet looks like the village or the play; the question mark flags him as one example of a Danish man.
explanation.definitionFit: To deign is to lower oneself to do something, synonymous with condescending.

clue.text: Brightly coloured vehicle belonging to the compiler

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
the compiler speaks as 'I', so what belongs to them is mine

explanation.surface: The setter boasts of a flashy car.
explanation.definitionFit: Carmine is a vivid crimson red, so this describes something brightly coloured.

clue.text: Comedian's practical intelligence

definitions.meaning: a funny person who makes clever jokes
common sense or quickness of mind

explanation.surface: A comic's down-to-earth cleverness.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', linking the two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a clever humorist and sharp good sense, two dictionary senses.

clue.text: Planner's course of action a Venetian painter announced

indicators.note: announced means the two words are said together, and their run-together sound gives the entry

parts.words: course of action a Venetian painter
parts.note: a tactic is a planned course of action; Titian was the great painter of Renaissance Venice

explanation.surface: A strategist's plan described alongside an Old Master.
explanation.walkthrough: Said quickly, the TIC of the first word and the TI of the painter's name blur into one, giving the sound of the strategist.
explanation.definitionFit: A tactician is someone skilled at planning moves, as in a battle or game.

clue.text: Bird from east of Germany, rolling in it!

parts.note: Ost is the German word for east
a slang phrase for being very wealthy

explanation.surface: A bird from eastern Germany wallowing in something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'east of Germany' reads as a region, but means the German word for east.
explanation.definitionFit: The ostrich is a large flightless African bird.

clue.text: Train in East Europe originally carrying old gold coin

indicators.note: carrying means the two letters hold the coin between them

parts.note: E is the compass abbreviation for east

indicators.note: originally takes just the opening letter of Europe

parts.note: a ducat was a gold coin used across Europe in the past

explanation.surface: A railway journey through eastern Europe with ancient money on board.
explanation.definitionFit: To train someone is to teach them, so it is a synonym for educating.

clue.text: Impressionist painter, one in outskirts of Muscat

indicators.note: in places the number inside those edges
outskirts of takes the edge letters of the city name, its first and last

explanation.surface: An Impressionist artist is found on the fringes of Oman's capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Claude Monet was the French painter whose work gave Impressionism its name.

clue.text: Ruffian removing last of water from receptacle in field?

indicators.note: removing says a letter is taken away from the receptacle

parts.note: a trough is a container for animal feed or water in a field

indicators.note: last of takes the final letter of water

explanation.surface: A thug empties a container in a meadow.
explanation.definitionFit: A tough is a rough, violent person, a noun synonym for ruffian.

clue.text: Clear divider of court at Wimbledon

definitions.meaning: to clear a sum after costs, as profit
the mesh strung across the middle of a tennis court

explanation.surface: Something clearly splits the tennis court at Wimbledon.
explanation.walkthrough: Wimbledon is the London home of the grass-court tennis championships.
explanation.definitionFit: Net means to earn as clear profit, and the net is the barrier dividing a tennis court.
